verdict.rationale: Proa documents its own tooling for performance and maintainability. Compile-time template validation and typed props, `--deny warnings` lints that catch rendering performance problems, `fmt --check --verify`, and paired HTML/Markdown views that flag missing fields all help keep a codebase correct and fast. Tiny island runtimes, streaming Suspense and page caching support speed. Nothing shows these hold up as an application, team or codebase grows. missing for 10: evidence of scaling to large codebases or teams (modular project structure, workspace or multi-crate guidance, build-time behavior at scale), and independent or hands-on corroboration of large production apps.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build large applications that stay fast and maintainable as my team and codebase grow

citations.quote: The macro validates the template at compile time, consolidates adjacent static markup, and preserves the correct escaping behavior for dynamic slots.
--deny warnings catches performance problems such as intermediate rendered strings, avoidable allocations, and async renderers that never await.
the fields passed to AboutPage are compile-time-checked props.
Adding a field or child to HTML can immediately flag its absence in a paired Markdown view, including when that view is not open.
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
